key_insight: The paper replaces non-associated Coulomb friction with an associated, GSM-compatible model by adding an internal variable tied to asperity-scale real contact area and plasticity.
engineering_relevance: This gives finite element contact analyses a thermodynamically consistent friction law that can reproduce Coulomb-like behavior while enabling minimization-based formulations.
method: Introduce an internal variable representing microscopic contact state / real area of contact.
Drive its evolution through irreversible plastic deformation of asperities to recover frictional response.
Provide both penalty and Lagrange-multiplier formulations for implementation.
evidence_signal: A 2D finite element penalty implementation matches classical Coulomb predictions on two benchmark tests.
watch_item: The model depends on calibrating an asperity-scale penetration depth and the penalty formulation may require careful tuning for robust contact enforcement.
paper_title: An associated model of Coulomb friction based on the real area of contact
